title: SEBI's LTCG Tax Proposal for FPIs: What it Means for Indian Investors
description: SEBI has proposed scrapping the 12.5% Long Term Capital Gains (LTCG) tax currently levied on Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs). This move aims to simplify th.

faq.q: What is Long Term Capital Gains (LTCG) tax?
faq.a: LTCG tax is levied on profits made from selling assets, like shares or property, that have been held for a specified long duration (typically over 12 months for equity). In India, for resident individuals, equity LTCG above ₹1 lakh is taxed at 10%.

FPIs are overseas entities or individuals who invest in the financial assets of a country other than their own. They typically invest in shares, bonds, and other securities, often with a shorter-term outlook than Foreign Direct Investors (FDIs).

faq.q: Will SEBI's proposal affect my LTCG tax as a resident Indian?
faq.a: No, SEBI's proposal to scrap the 12.5% LTCG tax is specifically for Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs). It does not directly change the existing 10% LTCG tax on equity gains above ₹1 lakh for resident Indian individuals.

faq.q: Why is SEBI proposing to scrap this tax for FPIs?
faq.a: SEBI's primary goal is to simplify the tax regime for foreign investors, making India a more attractive and competitive destination for global capital. This is expected to boost FPI inflows, enhance market liquidity, and support economic growth.

faq.q: If implemented, when would this change come into effect?
faq.a: This is currently a proposal from SEBI. For it to become law, it would need approval from the Ministry of Finance and potentially an amendment in the Income Tax Act. The exact timeline for implementation, if approved, is not yet determined.
